purpose: Test whether separating the TES heat capacity from one explicit local Si/substrate-membrane thermal node on the TES-to-bath path reduces or removes the shared c2 requirement across the 2024-12-05/06 adjacent-day noise spectra.

L_H.semantics: shared circuit inductance profile around the independently motivated physical scale; diagnostic prior, not a measured tolerance

C_tes_material_multiplier.semantics: TES-local heat capacity after separating the substrate/membrane node; referenced to the bare-bilayer material estimate but still treated as an effective local quantity

C_substrate_J_per_K.semantics: one symmetric local Si/substrate-membrane heat-capacity node per TES; the range includes the historical PoST C_tes scale but that historical number is not documented as an explicit silicon calorimetry result

G_tes_substrate_over_G_substrate_bath.semantics: shared conductance partition ratio. For each day G_tes-substrate and G_substrate-bath are derived so their series-equivalent conductance equals the existing G_tes-bath exactly.

guardrail: The added substrate node is a diagnostic lumped small-signal representation, not a geometrically resolved silicon model. It is placed in series on the TES-to-bath path because the reduced PoST model already represents that path by G_tes-bath. The DC series-equivalent conductance is held exactly equal to the original G_tes-bath, so the new freedom is a finite thermalization time scale rather than a changed DC thermal link. No independent steady-state substrate temperature or temperature-dependent two-link transport law is solved in this screen. A good fit does not prove the node is silicon; a surviving c2 still does not identify an electronics zero.
